# Code review: Express → Fastify migration (a8ca169…2153d07)

**Mode:** full review, committed range only (the range you gave), read-only. 122 files, +1335 −1020, of which about 1,080 lines are `yarn.lock`. This worktree has no `node_modules`, so nothing was run. Fastify, find-my-way and Nest adapter behaviour was checked against the installed copies in `~/Development/safe/cgw-1/node_modules`, which are newer patch/minor releases of the same majors.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | **Don't open yet.** There is one P1: every multisig transaction-detail request returns 404. |
| **Score** | Not computed. I didn't load the scoring formula, and I'd rather not invent a number. The P1 decides the verdict on its own. |
| **Fix first** | Pass `maxParamLength` when the Fastify adapter is built (`src/app.provider.ts:63`). |
| **Adjudicated** | 13 of 13 findings. 9 confirmed, 4 contested, 0 refuted. 2 were promoted from open deferrals and 1 was merged as a duplicate. |

**Corroboration:** later commits on `main` in `cgw-1` add `maxParamLength: 256`, `ignoreTrailingSlash: true` and a fix titled "allow empty JSON bodies" (#3266). Findings 1–3 below match those follow-ups.

## Findings by area

| Area | Findings |
|---|---|
| Regression | 1 P1 · 2 P3 · 1 appendix |
| Testing | 3 P3 · 1 appendix |
| Architecture, DRY | 1 appendix each |
| Security, bugs, performance | none (checked: trust proxy, cookie Max-Age in seconds, redirect argument order, Tenderly HMAC, rate-limit key cardinality, body limit) |
| KISS, conventions | only contested items (see "Not sure") |

## Must fix before opening

**1. P1 · Critical · Regression — multisig transaction IDs are unroutable.** `src/app.provider.ts:63`
- **What:** `new FastifyAdapter({ trustProxy, bodyLimit })` doesn't set `maxParamLength`, so find-my-way's default of 100 characters applies. Any path parameter longer than that doesn't match a route and returns Fastify's default 404.
- **Who it hits:** `GET chains/:chainId/transactions/:id` (`src/modules/transactions/routes/transactions.controller.ts:90`). A multisig ID (`multisig_<address>_<safeTxHash>`) is always 118 characters, so transaction details break for every multisig transaction on every chain. Express had no such limit.
- **Tests:** `get-transaction-by-id.transactions.controller.integration.spec.ts:547` expects 200 for exactly this ID, and the test app goes through the same adapter factory. It should fail at HEAD, but I couldn't run it to confirm.
- **Fix:** add `maxParamLength: 256` (about twice the longest real ID) at `src/app.provider.ts:63`, and run the transaction integration specs.

## Worth a ticket (or fold into this PR)

| # | P | Where | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | P3 | `src/app.provider.ts:63` (e.g. `src/modules/auth/routes/auth.controller.ts:153`) | Fastify returns 400 `FST_ERR_CTP_EMPTY_JSON_BODY` for `Content-Type: application/json` with an empty body. Express accepted it. This hits `POST /v1/auth/logout` and about 19 bodyless DELETE routes; the validator reproduced the 400. Existing tests miss it because supertest sends no content-type. Fix: register a JSON parser that tolerates empty bodies. |
| 3 | P3 | `src/app.provider.ts:63` | Routing is now strict about trailing slashes and case, where Express 5 was lenient. `/v1/chains/` and `/v1/Chains` now 404. The nginx proxy doesn't normalise URLs, and no test covers it (merged from a testing finding). The commit message says "behavioural parity intended". Fix: `ignoreTrailingSlash: true`, plus a deliberate decision on case sensitivity. |
| 4 | P3 | `src/routes/common/guards/rate-limit.guard.spec.ts:28` | The spec mocks an Express-shaped `route: { path }`, so the Fastify branch that builds the rate-limit key (`routeOptions.url`, `http-request.utils.ts:50`) is never tested. The address-book e2e test does go through Fastify, but it repeats one identical URL, so it can't tell route-template keys from raw-URL keys. |
| 5 | P3 | `src/app.provider.ts:38-56` | In the new `parseBodyLimit`, only `'1mb'` and `'8'` are tested. `kb`/`gb`, decimals and the throw on invalid input at line 50 are not. |
| 6 | appendix | `src/app.provider.ts:48` | The body-limit regex rejects `tb`/`pb` and `+1mb`, which the `bytes` library accepted. That would crash at boot, but no configured value uses those forms (only `'1mb'`), so it was downgraded to unlikely. |
| 7 | appendix/Low | `src/routes/common/interceptors/cache-control.interceptor.integration.spec.ts:58-62` | The "already sent" test passes even if the `!response.sent` guard at `cache-control.interceptor.ts:24` is removed. Both agents reproduced this: a `header()` call after `send()` has no effect on the wire. Assert that `header` is not called instead. |
| 8 | appendix | `src/app.provider.spec.ts:48-49` | The spec inlines `init()` + `ready()` instead of calling the new `initTestApplication` (`src/__tests__/test-app.provider.ts:23`). |
| 9 | appendix | `src/logging/utils.ts:4-10` | Logging now imports from `src/routes/common/http`, which reverses the dependency direction. Weakened to a nit: there's precedent (`src/domain/common/utils/signatures.ts:3`) and no written rule against it. |

## Not sure about these (contested: one agent upheld, one rejected)

- **Test-app configure loop duplicated** (`src/main.ts:21`, `src/__tests__/test-app.provider.ts:59`). This was promoted from an architecture deferral. The refuter points out the two loops iterate deliberately different lists (tests leave out the shutdown hooks).
- **Leftover Express branches in `RequestLike`** (`src/routes/common/http/http-request.utils.ts:7-57`). Narrowed: `get`, `header`, `path` and `route.path` are never present on any caller's request. `originalUrl`, `host`, `hostname` and `protocol` are live, including on the raw 404-middleware request that middie populates.
- **Stale comment** at `src/config/entities/configuration.ts:407-418`. It still says the value is parsed by Express body-parser / the `bytes` library and that Express trust-proxy resolves `req.ip`. The migration made that false, but the file isn't in the diff. The `'100kb'` default it mentions was already wrong before this PR.
- **Blank line after the SPDX header** in 7 files (e.g. `src/app.provider.ts:2`, `src/modules/auth/utils/auth-cookie.utils.ts:2`). The in-diff inconsistency is real, but about 25% of the repo already has this variant, biome ignores it, and no rule covers it. All changed files do have the SPDX header.

## Review limits

- **Nothing executed.** Fastify behaviour comes from nearby installed versions: 5.11.3 was inspected, 5.8.5 is pinned. Finding 1's failing test is inferred, not observed.
- **Cleanup proposals** (the "worth tidying" stage) were skipped because you asked for read-only.
- **No last-run state** was read or written, so there's no "since your last run" section.
- **Deferrals:** the testing pass's concern that `main.ts` reads raw config was closed with evidence (the validator returns the configuration unchanged). The security pass's concern about `getRoutePath` coverage is covered by finding 4.
